texts: good. the conditional becomes a fireable rule - the boiling, its sea-water medium and the threads all sit in the condition, and the forming is located in the cauldron and tied to each boiling.
good. the same fireable rule as the 'when' version, with the cauldron a single shared referent and 'a Keeper' read as the kind, so the rule ranges over every keeper.

mixed: the taking, the sea-water and the source pools are all captured, but capitalising a plural role word makes 'the Keepers' a bare proper name (like 'the Wrens'), carrying no link to the keeper kind your other sentences quantify over - so these Keepers connect to none of those rules. Write 'Keepers take the sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.' - lower-case and bare-plural, which records them as keepers and states the practice as the standing habit it is.

good. with bare kinds on both sides this lands as a single kind-to-kind fact at strength zero, faithful and directly queryable; be aware it is stored in a different shape from the event-based 'the cauldron yields mire-essence' rule, so a question about fresh water has to be asked in that kind-to-kind form.
